subject: GSS_PowerStrip

reply.subject: GSS_PowerStrip

observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: A long, narrow, rounded-corner bar in light warm-grey/beige plastic with a slightly mottled surface and a clean dark outline. Four round, dark-charcoal sockets with two pin holes each are evenly spaced along it, and a small glowing orange-red rocker switch sits at the right end. The bar sits in the lower part of a transparent canvas. Nothing extends past the outline: no cord, stub or tail.

The same bar at its native 256x128 size, lit variant. It spans about x 13-230 and y 57-100, so the right margin is wider than the left and the bar sits below the vertical centre. There are four dark two-pin sockets, a lit orange rocker at the right end and a transparent background.

A before/after comparison on a brown floor at 64 px/cell (top row) and 128 px/cell (bottom row). BEFORE: a small low-res grey strip with a black wire stub at its right end. AFTER lit and AFTER off: the new beige strip with two vertical orange extension cords plugged into sockets 1 and 3 (off panel: one more cord coming in diagonally from the upper left to socket 1). The orange feed cord leaves the right end cap horizontally. There is no vanilla human in this panel; for a floor decal the scale comes from the cell size.
The Off variant: identical bar, sockets, palette and outline, but the rocker switch is a dark unlit maroon instead of glowing orange.

A composite of the lit strip on the floor. Two orange cords come down from the north and end in brown rectangular plug heads that sit centred over sockets 1 and 3 and cover them completely; the plug bodies rise above the strip's top edge. Sockets 2 and 4 are visible and empty. The feed cord leaves the right end cap at mid-height, past the lit rocker, and runs off to the east. Plugs draw over the strip, and the feed cord meets the cap's edge.

A composite of the off strip. One cord arrives diagonally from the upper left, and its tilted plug head covers socket 1 at the left end. Two vertical cords have plug heads centred on sockets 3 and 4. Socket 2 is visible and empty, the rocker is dark, and the feed cord leaves the right end cap at mid-height.

CAMERA.seen: A flat floor decal seen from above. The card's Engine limits list top-down flat as intended for a floor decal; there is no round top or box to put in perspective.

BORE.seen: No open bore shows anywhere. The strip has no pipe, and the code-drawn cords end in plug heads, not open tube ends.

PORTS.seen: In both assembled panels each plug head sits centred on its socket and covers it completely (sockets 1 and 3 in the lit panel; 1, 3 and 4 in the off panel). The feed cord meets the right end cap at the bar's mid-height. Round 1's half-inserted look is gone.

LAYERS.seen: Plug heads and their cords draw over the strip, and the feed cord sits under or at the end cap with no overlap artifacts.

ROTATIONS.seen: A single decal with no facings. The lit and off variants are the same bar, sockets and palette, differing only in the rocker's glow.

SIGNATURE.seen: It reads at once as a 4-outlet power bar: four two-pin sockets and a rocker switch at the right end.

MATERIAL.seen: Beige/light-grey body with soft shading and a slight grain. It reads as moulded plastic; the sockets read as dark rubber or plastic.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The bar fits its 0.9-cell decal width. The off-centre margins are inherited on purpose so the code's socket constants stay valid, and the assembled views show plugs landing correctly.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparent background with no shadow, halo or floor patch (code-measured real alpha: true).

OURS.seen: New 256x128 painted art that is clearly different from the old 64x32 shipped texture shown in scale.png. No donor look.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The new texture is high-res, with no stubby black wire or any drawn cord. Plug heads drawn by code sit on the sockets, so the scene reads as one cable ending in a strip that other cables plug into.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 64 px/cell (scale.png top row) it reads as a light bar with dark sockets and plugs. At 32 px/cell it is about 29x6 px, small but still a light bar with dark dots, which is fine for a floor decal.

findings.where: scale.png top row, extrapolated to 32 px/cell
findings.seen: At 32 px/cell the sockets would be about 2-3 px dots and the rocker about 2 px, so the strip reduces to a pale sliver under the plugs.
findings.quote: does not read at 32 px/cell (advisory by the brief)
findings.fix: Keep the high-contrast dark sockets and the bright rocker so the strip still reads as a light bar with dark dots at 32 px per cell.

findings.seen: The body's faint mottled grain could read as a little stone-like at full zoom, though it reads as plastic at normal zoom.
findings.quote: Colour reads as material, not a coat of paint
findings.fix: The body is smooth moulded beige plastic with a soft sheen and very fine, even texture.

reply.needs_call_why: The assembled panels are an offline composite built from the C# constants, not an in-game capture. The class module says machine parts cannot reach ACCEPT on an offline mock, so the second look may answer 'unsure' on PORTS/LAYERS only because of the mock, not because of a visible defect. Judged on what is shown, the art and placement are correct.
proposals: For floor-decal machine parts (strips, junctures) whose placement is pure code arithmetic, let an offline composite built from the C# constants count as the assembled panel, or route 'unsure solely because assembled is a mock' to HOLD_INPUT rather than REGEN.
A floor-decal module that skips CAMERA/BORE (or answers them by rule), so a top-down decal is not judged against the 35-degree building camera.
